_comment: Crop-independent disease types. 'types' holds farmer-facing info per type; 'label_to_type' maps every dataset label (PlantVillage, PlantDoc, PlantWild v1/v2) to a type. Labels mapped to null are excluded (fruit-only or non-leaf problems). Shared by scripts/prepare_disease_types.py, training/disease_type/train.py and backend/app/services/disease_type_service.py.

management: No disease detected: keep scouting weekly
Maintain balanced fertilisation and irrigation

symptoms: Brown spots with concentric 'target' rings
Yellow halo around spots
Starts on older, lower leaves
management: Remove infected lower leaves
Mulch to stop soil splash onto leaves
Protective fungicide (chlorothalonil, mancozeb or copper) per label
Rotate away from the same crop family for 2-3 years

symptoms: Large dark, water-soaked patches that spread fast
White fuzzy growth on leaf undersides in humid weather
Brown lesions on stems
management: Act immediately: remove and destroy infected plants (do not compost)
Systemic + protectant fungicide (e.g. metalaxyl + mancozeb) per label before wet spells
Avoid overhead irrigation; improve airflow
Plant resistant varieties and certified seed

symptoms: Many small round or angular spots, often with dark borders or pale centres
Spots may merge and leaves yellow and drop
management: Remove and destroy spotted leaves and crop debris
Water at the base, not over the leaves
Protective fungicide (copper, chlorothalonil or mancozeb) per label
Rotate crops and space plants for airflow

symptoms: Long tan or grey-brown lesions or large dead areas on leaves
Lesions expand quickly in warm, humid weather
management: Plant resistant hybrids/varieties
Bury or remove infected residue; rotate crops
Fungicide at early disease onset if pressure is high

symptoms: Orange, reddish-brown or yellow powdery pustules
Pustules mostly on leaf undersides; leaves yellow and drop
management: Plant resistant varieties
Remove infected leaves and nearby alternate hosts where practical
Fungicide (triazoles, e.g. propiconazole/tebuconazole, or sulfur) at first pustules per label

symptoms: White to grey powdery patches on leaf surfaces
Leaves curl, yellow and dry out
management: Sulfur, potassium bicarbonate or neem oil at first white spots
Rotate fungicide groups to avoid resistance
Improve airflow; avoid excess nitrogen

symptoms: Yellow or pale patches on the upper leaf, limited by veins
Grey-purple fuzzy growth on the underside in humid conditions
management: Remove infected leaves; improve airflow and drainage
Avoid wetting foliage, especially in the evening
Copper or downy-mildew-specific fungicides (e.g. mancozeb, metalaxyl) per label

symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn dark, often with yellow halos
Angular spots limited by veins; leaves may tear or drop
management: Use disease-free seed and transplants
Copper-based bactericide sprays per label (fungicides alone do not work)
Do not work in wet plants; avoid overhead irrigation
Remove infected debris and rotate crops

symptoms: Light/dark green mosaic or mottling
Curled, crinkled, yellowed or stunted leaves
management: No cure: remove and destroy infected plants
Control insect vectors (whiteflies, aphids) e.g. with sticky traps, neem or labelled insecticides
Use virus-free seed and resistant varieties
Disinfect tools and wash hands after handling infected plants

symptoms: Olive-green to dark velvety spots on leaves
Cracked, corky spots on fruit
management: Rake and destroy fallen leaves
Protective fungicide (captan or sulfur) from bud break per label
Plant scab-resistant varieties; prune for airflow

symptoms: Brown leaf spots with dark borders ('frogeye')
Shrivelled black fruit (mummies)
Cankers on branches or canes
management: Remove mummified fruit and cankered wood
Fungicide (captan, mancozeb or myclobutanil) during the growing season per label
Prune for airflow

symptoms: Dark, sunken lesions on leaves, stems or fruit
Lesions may show pink/orange spore masses when wet
management: Remove infected plant parts and debris
Avoid overhead irrigation
Protective fungicide (copper, chlorothalonil) per label
Use clean planting material

symptoms: Pale yellow spots on the upper leaf
Olive-green to brown velvety mould underneath
management: Lower humidity: ventilate greenhouses, space plants
Remove infected leaves
Fungicide (chlorothalonil, copper) per label; resistant varieties

symptoms: Grey fuzzy mould on leaves, flowers or fruit
Soft brown rot of tissue
management: Remove infected tissue promptly
Improve airflow; avoid wet foliage
Fungicide at flowering per label

symptoms: Fine yellow/white speckling (stippling) on leaves
Fine webbing on leaf undersides; leaves bronze and dry
management: Spray leaf undersides with water or insecticidal soap / neem oil
Release predatory mites
Use a miticide (e.g. abamectin) per label for heavy infestations

symptoms: Blotchy, asymmetrical yellow mottling
Small, lopsided, bitter fruit
management: No cure: remove infected trees
Control the Asian citrus psyllid
Plant certified disease-free stock; report to your extension office

symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' yellow/red patches between leaf veins
Dark spotting on berries; sudden vine collapse
management: Prune in dry weather and protect large cuts
Remove and destroy dead wood
Replace severely affected vines

symptoms: Leaves wilt even when soil is moist
Yellowing and browning of whole branches; plant collapse
management: Remove and destroy wilted plants
Control insect vectors (e.g. cucumber beetles)
Use resistant varieties and clean planting material; rotate crops

symptoms: Swollen galls or heads filled with black powdery spores
management: Remove galls before they burst
Use treated or certified seed and resistant varieties
Rotate crops

symptoms: Thickened, puckered, red-purple curled leaves in spring
management: Copper or lime-sulfur spray when trees are dormant (late autumn / before bud swell)
Remove curled leaves; keep trees vigorous

symptoms: Diamond-shaped grey-centred lesions with brown borders
Neck rot causing empty panicles
management: Resistant varieties
Avoid excess nitrogen; keep fields flooded evenly
Fungicide (e.g. tricyclazole) per label at early infection
